lines.say: A hundred dollars in 2015. Change it into your local money, and wait ten years.
Here is what it is worth in dollars, every year.
Jordan, Saudi Arabia and the UAE stay at a hundred. Their money is pegged to the dollar.
Syria's pound keeps collapsing in the civil war.
Turkey's lira slides every single year.
Lebanon's banks freeze in 2019. Then the pound falls off a cliff.
Iran's official rate is frozen, so it tells us nothing. No data.
The euro ends near a hundred and two. The British pound, eighty six.
Which currency surprised you? Tell me in the comments.
And Israel, after two years of war?
The shekel. It peaks at a hundred and twenty in 2021, and ends at a hundred and twelve dollars and sixty cents.

sources.label: World Bank, official exchange rate PA.NUS.FCRF, yearly average

caption_en:
Ten years, eleven currencies. The winner went through two years of war.

US$100 changed into local money in 2015, measured back in dollars (World Bank official exchange rates, yearly averages):
Israel (shekel) 2025: $112.60
Euro 2025: $101.84
Jordan, Saudi Arabia, UAE: $100 (pegged to the dollar)
UK pound 2025: $86.18
Egypt 2025: $15.62
Syria 2022 (latest): $9.46
Turkey 2025: $6.89
Lebanon 2025: $1.68
Iran: no data (the official rate stayed frozen at 42,000 rial while the market rate moved)

Exchange rates are not wealth, and a strong shekel also hurts Israeli exporters and tourism. This is not financial advice.

Source: World Bank, World Development Indicators, PA.NUS.FCRF (official exchange rate, LCU per US$, period average), 2015 to 2025. Value = 100 x rate in 2015 / rate in that year.
